pr_title: Fix error reporting for objects with unsupported property types
pr_body:
Makes a couple of changes:

* Reverts changes in unsupported property error reporting from #66169 following feedback from the aspnetcore team. Also fixes a related issue concerning JsonPath reporting in failed dictionary key deserialization.
* Refactors the dictionary tests to use Xunit theories instead of bespoke inheritance and integrates them into the `CollectionTests` suite.

Fix #66590.

issue_context.title: Quarantine ReadAsync_WithAllowInputFormatterExceptionMessages_RegistersJsonInputExceptionsAsInputFormatterException
issue_context.body:
# Investigation

Cause: Previously the STJ exception message referred to the specific property that couldn't be converted (i.e., the JSON value could not be converted to `System.Decimal`) whereas now it refers to the enclosing type (i.e., saying we can't convert the JSON to `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Formatters.SystemTextJsonInputFormatterTest+User`).

This failure starts to happen if we update to the latest runtime, so is very likely due to a change of runtime behavior. I did a bit of digging and it looks pretty likely that the underlying cause is this PR: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/66169 which was merged last week.

It looks like the same thing on the grounds that in that PR, they also had to change their tests to stop asserting that the message refers to a property type, and start asserting that it refers to the enclosing type instead: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/66169#discussion_r819134061

To me, the new STJ behavior looks less desirable than the old STJ behavior, since previously it was telling you which specific property type wasn't convertible, whereas now it just generically tells you about the parent object type. So this might turn out to be a STJ regression that should be fixed. However, the comment from @eiriktsarpalis specifically says that the old behavior was incorrect and the new behavior is correct, so I can't assume this is a regression.

@Tratcher @halter73 I'm not certain who owns this part of the product (CODEOWNERS claims it's @dotnet/aspnet-blazor-eng, which doesn't seem right). Could the owner of this test please figure out whether we should change the test, or whether to report this as a regression to the STJ runtime team?

In the meantime I'll make a quarantining PR but we might want to halt that process if we decide it's a runtime regression.

## Failing Test(s)

Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Formatters.SystemTextJsonInputFormatterTest.ReadAsync_WithAllowInputFormatterExceptionMessages_RegistersJsonInputExceptionsAsInputFormatterException

comments: @rafikiassumani-msft would be the owner of this area, since its web API

The change came about during essential infrastructural refactoring of STJ internals. The exception surfaces from the converter factory for the parent type and as such it made sense to me at the time to report the parent type itself rather than the property type that is being processed (note: this is doing reflection-based metadata processing rather than performing deserialization at that particular stage).

This might have made sense given [STJ's own test coverage](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/66169#r819134061) but might be less so in other scenaria. Could you share a link to the failing unit test as well as the full expected and actual error message strings? Thanks.

Sure. The failing test is [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Formatters.SystemTextJsonInputFormatterTest.ReadAsync_WithAllowInputFormatterExceptionMessages_RegistersJsonInputExceptionsAsInputFormatterException](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/src/Mvc/Mvc.Core/test/Formatters/SystemTextJsonInputFormatterTest.cs#L133), specifically the case for "age" where it's trying to parse as System.Decimal.

Expected error: `The JSON value could not be converted to System.Decimal`
Actual error: `The JSON value could not be converted to Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Formatters.SystemTextJsonInputFormatterTest+User`.

review_comments: Ensures that the right `JsonPropertyInfo` is surfaced depending on whether we serialize the key or the value for the dictionary.
Is this covered by tests? I didn't see any "property name + exception" test changes here that were dictionary-specific.

Yes. See the changes to the `ThrowOnInvalidFormat` test in the first commit: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/67109/commits/fb35427bfeb0aaae03896c56f833c43c705e2c8d#diff-e978d8822ab16e2ef9eb42029b8cfe1bb27717da7f7b6702ac864de3fd5c3a38
Moves this assignment assignment _before_ the call to `ReadAsPropertyNameCore` so that the correct JsonPath is surfaced in case of an error.
Would it be better to just not include this file in the csproj instead of the whole-file #if? Not sure what we are doing elsewhere in similar cases.
Good point, we're following a similar pattern in other unsupported tests. I suspect it's because both projects are importing the `Common` source files from a shared `targets` file.
Ensures any unsupported key type errors are forced at the start of serialization.
I see - removing this class and replacing with theories.
There's a lot of changes in this file - I did a few spot checks to ensure the tests are still there, but didn't verify everything.
